segs: There's a village in Dorset with a name so bad, people kept stealing the sign.
And it's been called that for almost a thousand years.
It's in the Domesday Book, from ten eighty-six.
The name roughly means the farm on the stream used as an open sewer.
Then, every two or three years, the sign vanished.
And every time, the council paid for a new one.
So in twenty ten, the residents had enough.
More than half the households chipped in twenty pounds each.
They bought a one-and-a-half tonne block of stone, and carved the name into it.
Two years later, a survey named it Britain's worst place name.
They didn't change it. They made it impossible to move.
